场景一：一个创业团队的融资没谈成，原计划已经不成立。负责人第一次全员会上最有用的，也许就是像那句“任务是让全体队员抵达陆地”一样，用一句话说清新的目标：现在要做到什么，怎么算做到。

Everything here comes from Shackleton's own narrative (this piece uses the OCR text of the 1920 printing): the account of the participant who led the party, with no other member's diary for comparison. The OCR carries errors, and quotations are drawn only from clean stretches. Every figure in the piece comes from that account and has not been independently verified. The rescue that followed is not covered here.

new.zh: 原计划要宏大得多：横穿队伍立刻出发，踏上1800英里的行程，希望在五个月内穿越极点，抵达罗斯海一侧的基地。船被压毁之后，任务换成了另一件事——让全队上岸。
new.en: The plan he began with was far grander: "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Eighteen hundred miles, the Pole, a base on the far side of the continent. Once the ice had crushed Endurance, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.

new.zh: 船被冰困了281天，随浮冰向西北漂了570多英里。弃船时他算过他们的处境：离保利特岛还有346英里，那是最近一处可能找到食物和住处的地方。岛上有一座1902年瑞典探险队盖的小屋，里面存着阿根廷救援船留下的物资；这批物资他再熟悉不过，正是他当年在伦敦替阿根廷政府采购的。向西最近的冰障约180英里，可到了那里，离保利特岛仍有约360英里，而冰障上没有任何活命的办法。
new.en: The ship had been locked in the ice for 281 days and had drifted more than 570 miles to the north-west. When they left her he worked out where they stood. They were 346 miles from Paulet Island, "the nearest point where there is any possibility of finding food and shelter." A small hut built there by the Swedish expedition in 1902 held stores left by the Argentine relief ship, and he knew those stores well: he had bought them himself in London on behalf of the Argentine Government. The nearest barrier to the west was about 180 miles away, but a party going there would still be about 360 miles from Paulet Island, and "there would be no means of sustaining life on the barrier."

edits.reason: Second pass (more evidence): S-E9 where they stood (281 days, 346 miles to Paulet Island, stores he had bought); Dump Camp paragraph moves into the story; transition sentence removed.

edits.new: 从抛弃营到海洋营
edits.reason: Story now runs from Dump Camp to Ocean Camp.

edits.new: From Dump Camp to Ocean Camp

new.zh: 在被他们称为抛弃营的地方，装备经历了一次大幅筛选。他决定给每人发一整套全新的 Burberry 外衣和内衣，再加新袜子；同时定下规矩：个人物品不得超过两磅，除了最必需的东西，一律不上路。用他的原话，负担不起多余的重量。
new.en: At a place they named Dump Camp, the equipment went through a severe weeding-out. He decided to issue each man a complete new set of Burberrys — Burberry coats — and underclothing, along with a supply of new socks. At the same time he fixed the rule: "personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man," which meant nothing but bare necessaries would go on the march. In his words, they could not afford to cumber themselves with unnecessary weight.

new.zh: 于是有了那个读完忘不掉的细节：金币被扔掉，照片被留下；他还从王后赠给船的那本圣经上撕下扉页，那一页上有她亲笔写的字。
new.en: And so the detail that stays with you: "sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept." He tore the fly-leaf out of the Bible the Queen had given to the ship, the page with her own writing on it.

new.zh: 真正压人的是船。两条小艇连同装备和底下的雪橇，每条都超过一吨。他写道，雪橇是最薄弱的一环：载着这样的重量走在粗糙的压力冰上，几乎不可能不被压碎，而前面这样的冰面大概还有300英里。
new.en: The real weight was the boats. Each of them, with its gear and the sledges beneath it, weighed more than a ton. "The sledges were the point of weakness." It seemed almost hopeless, he wrote, to keep them from smashing under their loads on rough pressure-ice "which stretched ahead of us for probably 300 miles."

new.zh: 第一天的走法是接力。开路的小队拿着镐和铲，在冰脊间为拉船的雪橇凿出一条路；七组狗队把雪橇往前拉半英里，再折回去拉其余的雪橇；沃斯利管着两条船，十五个人拉，也得分段倒运。他们跨过两道正在张开的冰缝，缝里有虎鲸探出头来。到下午5点，他们向北偏西北走了一英里。
new.en: The first day's method was the relay. A pioneer party with picks and shovels broke a road through the pressure-ridges for the sledges carrying the boats. The seven dog teams "took their sledges forward for half a mile, then went back for the other sledges." Worsley took charge of the two boats, "with fifteen men hauling, and these also had to be relayed." They crossed two opening cracks with killer whales pushing their snouts through, and by 5 p.m. they had covered a mile, north-north-west.

new.zh: 行军的账很难看。一天下来，直线只前进了约一英里；为了绕开障碍，实际走过的距离至少两英里；分批搬运、来回接力，又把当天走过的路程推到了六英里，有几组狗队至少跑了十英里。当晚只能在平坦但又年轻又咸的冰上扎营。夜里虎鲸一直在喷气，凌晨2点，离营地约20英尺处裂开一道缝。他写道，脚下的冰薄得足以让虎鲸撞破，可近处没有别的地方能扎营，只好冒这个险。
new.en: The arithmetic of the march made ugly reading. They had gained about one mile in a direct line; the detours made the ground actually covered at least two miles, and the relays pushed the day's marching up to six. Some of the dog teams had covered at least ten miles. That night they camped on flat ice that "proved to be young and salty." The killers were blowing all night, and at 2 a.m. a crack opened about 20 feet from the camp. The ice was thin enough for the killers to break through, he wrote, "but there was no other camping-ground within our reach and we had to take the risk."

new.zh: 第二天早上雪下得极大，几十码外就看不清。他决定不拔营：在破碎的浮冰上很难找到路，把船弄进危险的位置可能酿成大祸。有人折回抛弃营取木头和鲸脂生火；天晴一些后，他和沃斯利往西探路，找到一块大浮冰，至少还能再往西北走一英里。午饭后，他们拔营继续。
new.en: The next morning "the snow was falling so heavily that we could not see more than a few score yards ahead, and I decided not to strike camp. A path over the shattered floes would be hard to find, and to get the boats into a position of peril might be disastrous." Men went back to Dump Camp for wood and blubber for the fire. When the weather cleared a little, he and Worsley went prospecting to the west and found a large floe that offered a fairly good road for at least another mile to the north-west. After lunch they struck camp.

new.zh: 下午开路顺利得多。两组狗拉着小艇出发，只需帮一次手；他写道，十四条狗干得和十八个人一样好，甚至更好。十几个人用镐和铲，十分钟就能在一道约14英尺高的冰脊上凿出一条还算平整的路。
new.en: The afternoon went better. Two dog teams were hitched to the cutter and "started off in splendid style. They needed to be helped only once; indeed fourteen dogs did as well or even better than eighteen men." A dozen men with picks and shovels could cut a road through a ridge about 14 feet high in ten minutes and leave a smooth, or comparatively smooth, path behind them.

new.zh: 可总账没有变。湿雪很深，又要不断停下来凿路，他们向目标走了将近一英里，倒运和绕路又让实际路程接近六英里。看到大家都已筋疲力尽，他下令在两条船的背风处搭帐篷。搭帐篷时，一名水手在一条船里的帆布上发现一小洼雪水，每人只够抿一口；他引了一位队员日记里的话：喝过更干净的水，但很少有来得这么是时候的。
new.en: The overall account did not change. Through wet, deep snow, with constant halts to cut a road, they "managed to march the best part of a mile towards our goal, though the relays and the deviations again made the actual distance travelled nearer six miles." Seeing that the men were all exhausted, he had the tents pitched in the lee of the two boats. While they were at it, a sailor found a little pool of thawed snow on a sail lying in one of the boats: just a sip each. He quoted what one man wrote in his diary: "One has seen and tasted cleaner, but seldom more opportunely found water."

new.zh: 苦干四天之后的第二天，天冷而平静，还是那种湿雪。他看清了两件事：以眼下松软的雪面，加上四天苦干换来的那点成果，走不了多远；同时，附近有可能开出水道，那样就能划船向西北方向去找陆地。两件事合起来指向同一个决定——找一块更结实的浮冰扎营，等条件更有利时再做第二次挣脱冰牢的尝试。
new.en: The next day, after four days of hard effort, broke cold and still, with the same wet snow. In the clearing light he could see the situation plainly. With the surface as loose as it was, and given how little they had to show for four days of strenuous effort, they would never get any great distance. And there was a second possibility to weigh: leads might open close to them, which would let them row north-west to where they might find land. The two considerations pointed one way. He decided to find a more solid floe, camp there, and stay until conditions were more favourable for a second attempt to escape from their icy prison.

new.zh: 他们把帐篷和全部家当搬到一块又厚又重的老浮冰上，距沉船约一英里半，在那里扎下营，取名海洋营。
new.en: Tents and everything else were moved to a thick, heavy old floe about one and a half miles from the wreck, and there they made their camp. They called it Ocean Camp.

new.zh: 光是把两条船挪过去就费尽了力气。雪面糟透了，他们从没见过这样的冰面：人有时陷到齐臀深，到处的雪都有两英尺厚。
new.en: Shifting the two boats there took the utmost effort. The surface was terrible, like nothing any of them had seen before: "We were sinking at times up to our hips, and everywhere the snow was two feet deep."

new.zh: 扎营后，他决定尽量省下宝贵的雪橇口粮，留给那趟必然要来的小艇航行，平时几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活。他派人回抛弃营搜罗衣物、烟草之类，可几天大雪，加上融化下陷，留在那里的许多东西已经不见了。
new.en: Once in camp, "I decided to conserve our valuable sledging rations, which would be so necessary for the inevitable boat journey, as much as possible, and to subsist almost entirely on seals and penguins." A party went back to Dump Camp for clothing, tobacco and whatever else they could find, but heavy snow and the thaw had swallowed a good many of the things left there.

new.zh: 这块浮冰起初约一英里见方，后来越裂越小，成了他们将近两个月的家。两个月里，他们常回到沉船附近，捞回许多衣物、食物，还有少数私人物品。他写道，那些东西当初是怀着轻松的乐观，以为可以一路冲过移动的冰面奔向安全，才打算丢在几英里之外的。
new.en: This floating lump of ice, about a mile square at first and later splitting into smaller and smaller pieces, was their home for nearly two months. In that time they went back again and again to the wreck and retrieved clothing, food "and some few articles of personal value which in our light-hearted optimism we had thought to leave miles behind us on our dash across the moving ice to safety."

new.zh: 后来他们又换了营地，叫耐心营，在那里住了将近三个半月。
new.en: Later they moved camp again, to a place they called Patience Camp, and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

edits.reason: Second pass: removed duplicates (story.0 repeated hook.0; story.1–2 repeated the Dump Camp paragraph); added the march day by day from S-E10–S-E15 (boats over a ton, relays, first night, the morning he did not strike camp, cutting roads, exhaustion) and after the decision S-E16–S-E18 (boats, rations, Dump Camp losses, two months, 'light-hearted optimism').

new.zh: 一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；午后天晴，探到一块好走的浮冰，又继续走。两次决定看的是同样的东西：眼前这段路找不找得到、值不值得把船带进去冒险。海洋营的不同在于，这一次他把等待写成了一个计划：营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望——附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地——等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。
new.en: One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared in the afternoon and a good floe turned up, they moved on. Both decisions weighed the same things: could a road be found, and was it worth taking the boats into danger to use it? What set Ocean Camp apart is that this time he wrote the waiting down as a plan. The camp went onto a more solid floe, the reasoning carried a specific hope (leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west), and a second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.

new.zh: 还有一处值得注意（作者的解读）：沙克尔顿后来用“轻松的乐观”来形容最初那场冲过移动冰面奔向安全的打算。停下之后，他们反而能一趟趟回到沉船边，捞回衣物、食物和当初丢下的东西，又改吃海豹和企鹅，把雪橇口粮留给后面的小艇航行。在这份记述里，停下不只是不再消耗，也是把资源重新收拢的时间。
new.en: One more thing is worth noticing, and again it is the author's reading. Shackleton later called the first plan, the dash across the moving ice to safety, a piece of "light-hearted optimism". Once they stopped, they could go back to the wreck again and again for clothing, food and the things they had left behind, and they switched to seals and penguins so that the sledging rations could be kept for the boat journey ahead. In his account, stopping was not only a halt to the drain; it was time to gather their resources again.

new.zh: 另一种解释是关于取舍的标准（作者推断）：金币在冰上派不上用场，照片和一页有亲笔字的扉页也换不来什么，但后两者被留下了。他在这几段里没有说明原因；也许那道上限筛的只是重量，也许只是个人偏好，两种说法都超出了他写下的内容。
new.en: A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. Gold coins were of no use on the ice; the photographs and a page with the Queen's handwriting could not buy anything either, yet those were the things kept. He gives no reason in these passages. Perhaps the limit screened only for weight; perhaps it was personal preference. Both go beyond what he wrote.

new.zh: 作者提出的替代选择（他没有写自己考虑过这些）：比如把队伍分成两支，一支维持最低限度的探路，一支守营保存体力；或者先派少数人轻装去试水道。这类做法都要把队伍拆开。列在这里只是想说明，那天的决定不是唯一的可能，却和当时手里的条件对得上。
new.en: Then there are alternatives the author raises for the sake of argument; nothing suggests Shackleton weighed them himself. The party could have been split in two, one half keeping up a minimal reconnaissance while the other held the camp and conserved its strength. Or a few men might have gone ahead lightly loaded, to feel out the leads. Both would have meant splitting the party. They are listed here only to show that the decision of that day was not the only possibility, though it did match the conditions in front of them.

edits.reason: Second pass: old analysis.0 claimed the wording 'let the party bank its strength' (unsupported); replaced by the day-two non-move (S-E13) and the 'light-hearted optimism' reading (S-E18), both labelled as the author's.

new.zh: 本篇的全部过程都出自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（这里用的是1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述，其中有些段落像是当时的日记。没有取得其他队员的日记作对照，营地里别人怎么想、是否同意这个决定，证据里没有，本篇也不替他们猜测心理。文中那句“喝过更干净的水”出自一位未具名队员的日记，是经沙克尔顿转引的。
new.en: Everything in this piece comes from Shackleton's own narrative, read here through the OCR text of the 1920 printing: the account of a participant who led the party, parts of which read like a contemporary diary. No other member's diary has been brought in for comparison. What the rest of the camp thought, and whether anyone questioned the decision, is not in the evidence, and this piece does not put feelings in their mouths. The line about the sip of water comes from an unnamed member's diary, as quoted by Shackleton.

new.zh: 文本是 OCR，有讹字，引用只取清晰片段，个别有讹字的词不加引号照抄。所有数字——1800英里、281天、346英里、两磅、一吨、一英里、六英里、一英里半、两个月、三个半月——都出自他的记述，未与别的记录核对。本篇也不写此后获救的过程，那部分不在这份证据包的覆盖范围内。
new.en: The text is machine-read, and it carries errors. Quotations are taken only from clean stretches; a few damaged words are reproduced without quotation marks. All the figures — 1,800 miles, 281 days, 346 miles, two pounds, a ton, one mile, six miles, one and a half miles, two months, three and a half months — come from his account and have not been checked against any other record. Nor does this piece tell the story of the rescue that followed; that falls outside the evidence gathered here.
